001package com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog;
002
003import org.apache.commons.lang3.Validate;
004import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.annotations.HistoryLogProps;
005import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.helpers.Bytes;
006
007import java.util.Arrays;
008
009/**
010 * The response the pump sent to a signed CONTROL request, written immediately after the
011 * {@link ControlRequestHistoryLog} for that request (its {@code requestOpCode} is this record's
012 * {@code responseOpCode} minus one in 3692/3692 records across both capture sets).
013 *
014 * <p>The class name is provisional: Tandem's cloud export and the Mobi app's HistoryLogType enum
015 * do not name this opcode.
016 *
017 * <p>Only some commands are answered with this record. Observed response opcodes: 133
018 * UserInteraction, 135 SetMaxBolusLimit, 137 SetMaxBasalLimit, 155 ResumePumping, 157
019 * SuspendPumping, 167 StopTempRate, 195 CgmHighLowAlert, 197 CgmRiseFallAlert, 199
020 * CgmOutOfRangeAlert, 211 SetQuickBolusSettings, 213 SetPumpAlertSnooze, 215 ChangeTimeDate, 217
021 * SetBgReminder, 221 SetSiteChangeReminder, 223 SetLowInsulinAlert, 225 SetAutoOffAlert, 229
022 * SetPumpSounds, 237 SetActiveIDP and 245 PlaySound. SetTempRate is answered with
023 * {@link SetTempRateResponseHistoryLog} instead; the cartridge/fill commands and
024 * DismissNotification use other opcodes as well.
025 *
026 * <p>Byte 11 and bytes 13-25 are zero in every Mobi record examined; they are kept as raw
027 * accessors. See https://github.com/jwoglom/pumpx2/issues/145.
028 */
029
030/**
031 * History log record Control Response, opCode 300, size 26.
032 *
033 * <br>
034 *
035 * The response the pump sent to a signed CONTROL request, written immediately after the
036 * {@link ControlRequestHistoryLog} for that request (its {@code requestOpCode} is this record's
037 * {@code responseOpCode} minus one in 3692/3692 records across both capture sets).
038 *
039 * <p>The class name is provisional: Tandem's cloud export and the Mobi app's HistoryLogType enum
040 * do not name this opcode.
041 *
042 * <p>Only some commands are answered with this record. Observed response opcodes: 133
043 * UserInteraction, 135 SetMaxBolusLimit, 137 SetMaxBasalLimit, 155 ResumePumping, 157
044 * SuspendPumping, 167 StopTempRate, 195 CgmHighLowAlert, 197 CgmRiseFallAlert, 199
045 * CgmOutOfRangeAlert, 211 SetQuickBolusSettings, 213 SetPumpAlertSnooze, 215 ChangeTimeDate, 217
046 * SetBgReminder, 221 SetSiteChangeReminder, 223 SetLowInsulinAlert, 225 SetAutoOffAlert, 229
047 * SetPumpSounds, 237 SetActiveIDP and 245 PlaySound. SetTempRate is answered with
048 * {@link SetTempRateResponseHistoryLog} instead; the cartridge/fill commands and
049 * DismissNotification use other opcodes as well.
050 *
051 * <p>Byte 11 and bytes 13-25 are zero in every Mobi record examined; they are kept as raw
052 * accessors. See https://github.com/jwoglom/pumpx2/issues/145.
053 *
054 * 
055 * <table border='1'>
056 * <caption>Message properties:</caption>
057 * <tr><th>&nbsp;<code>opCode</code>&nbsp;</th><td>&nbsp;<code>300</code>&nbsp;</td></tr>
058 * <tr><th>&nbsp;<code>displayName</code>&nbsp;</th><td>&nbsp;<code>"Control Response"</code>&nbsp;</td></tr>
059 * <tr><th>&nbsp;<code>internalName</code>&nbsp;</th><td>&nbsp;<code>""</code>&nbsp;</td></tr>
060 * </table>
061 */@HistoryLogProps(
062    opCode = 300,
063    displayName = "Control Response",
064    internalName = ""
065)
066public class ControlResponseHistoryLog extends HistoryLog {
067
068    private int responseOpCode;
069    private int unknown11;
070    private int status;
071    private byte[] unknownTail;
072
073    public ControlResponseHistoryLog() {}
074    public ControlResponseHistoryLog(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, int responseOpCode, int unknown11, int status, byte[] unknownTail) {
075        super(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum);
076        this.cargo = buildCargo(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum, responseOpCode, unknown11, status, unknownTail);
077        this.responseOpCode = responseOpCode;
078        this.unknown11 = unknown11;
079        this.status = status;
080        this.unknownTail = Arrays.copyOfRange(this.cargo, 13, 26);
081    }
082
083    public ControlResponseHistoryLog(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, int responseOpCode, int status) {
084        this(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum, responseOpCode, 0, status, new byte[13]);
085    }
086
087    public ControlResponseHistoryLog(int responseOpCode, int status) {
088        this(0, 0, responseOpCode, status);
089    }
090
091    public int typeId() {
092        return 300;
093    }
094
095    /**
096     * <table border="1">
097     * <caption>Parsed fields for ControlResponseHistoryLog:</caption>
098     * <tr><td><code>responseOpCode</code></td><td><code>raw[10] &amp; 0xFF</code></td></tr>
099     * <tr><td><code>unknown11</code></td><td><code>raw[11] &amp; 0xFF</code></td></tr>
100     * <tr><td><code>status</code></td><td><code>raw[12] &amp; 0xFF</code></td></tr>
101     * <tr><td><code>unknownTail</code></td><td><code>Arrays.copyOfRange(raw, 13, 26)</code></td></tr>
102     * </table>
103     */
104    public void parse(byte[] raw) {
105        Validate.isTrue(raw.length == 26);
106        this.cargo = raw;
107        parseBase(raw);
108        this.responseOpCode = raw[10] & 0xFF;
109        this.unknown11 = raw[11] & 0xFF;
110        this.status = raw[12] & 0xFF;
111        this.unknownTail = Arrays.copyOfRange(raw, 13, 26);
112    }
113
114    public static byte[] buildCargo(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, int responseOpCode, int unknown11, int status, byte[] unknownTail) {
115        Validate.isTrue(unknownTail.length == 13, "unknownTail must be 13 bytes");
116        return HistoryLog.fillCargo(Bytes.combine(
117            HistoryLog.typeIdBytes(300, 0),
118            Bytes.toUint32(pumpTimeSec),
119            Bytes.toUint32(sequenceNum),
120            new byte[]{ (byte) responseOpCode, (byte) unknown11, (byte) status },
121            unknownTail));
122    }
123
124    /**
125     * The opcode of the response the pump sent, as an unsigned byte (the pumpX2 response
126     * {@code opCode} ANDed with 0xFF), which is the request's opcode plus one: for example 167
127     * is StopTempRateResponse and 155 is ResumePumpingResponse.
128     *
129     * @return the unsigned opcode of the response
130     */
131    public int getResponseOpCode() {
132        return responseOpCode;
133    }
134
135    /**
136     * The status byte of that response: 0 on success. Every nonzero value checked against the
137     * app log matched a response that reported a failure (for example a ResumePumping request
138     * rejected with status 1 and retried successfully a second later); StopTempRate responses
139     * logged as successful all read 0 here (1734/1734).
140     *
141     * @return the response status, 0 for success
142     */
143    public int getStatus() {
144        return status;
145    }
146
147    /**
148     * @return byte 11, which was 0 in every record examined
149     */
150    public int getUnknown11() {
151        return unknown11;
152    }
153
154    /**
155     * Bytes 13-25. They are zero on the Mobi. In 17 t:slim X2 records answering
156     * UserInteraction (response opcode 133), bytes 15-17 of the record (index 2-4 here) held the
157     * low 24 bits of the record's own pumpTimeSec; their purpose is unknown.
158     *
159     * @return a copy of bytes 13-25
160     */
161    public byte[] getUnknownTail() {
162        return Arrays.copyOf(unknownTail, unknownTail.length);
163    }
164}
